title: derbies() returns 0 Clássico Mineiro matches (should be 69) — hardcoded key "atletico" is not in the alias registry
evidence: soccer_data.py:79 DERBIES has ("cruzeiro", "atletico", "Clássico Mineiro"); normalize_team("atletico") -> 'atletico', which is absent from CANONICAL_ALIASES/TEAM_DISPLAY, while every real Mineiro row normalizes to 'atletico mg' (data/kaggle: 704 "Atlético-MG" + 424 "Atletico Mineiro" + 418 "Atletico-MG"). Verified by loading the store: derbies() yields Clássico Mineiro=0 while _filter(team='cruzeiro', opponent='Atlético-MG') yields 69. All 11 other derby pairs resolve. Not caught by test_brazilian_soccer.py:312 test_derbies_2023, which only asserts len(res) > 0 over the whole list. NOTE: derbies is beyond-spec (TASK.md sample question "Show me all derbies in 2023"); it maps to NO pinned REQUIREMENTS.json id, so this does not reduce the 12/12 pinned requirement_coverage.
suggestion: Use "atletico mg" (the canonical key, matching "athletico" -> 'atletico pr' used on the Atletiba row) in the DERBIES tuple, and assert per-pair non-empty results in the derby test.

title: derbies() applies `limit` per rival pair, not to the returned list
evidence: soccer_data.py:797 loops over DERBIES and calls m.head(limit) inside the loop, so the documented "limit – max matches to return" (mcp_server.py:200) is a per-pair cap. Observed: derbies() with default limit=50 returns 447 matches (8 pairs capped at exactly 50), not 50. Beyond-spec tool; maps to no pinned requirement id.
suggestion: Accumulate across pairs and slice once at the end, or rename the parameter to per_derby_limit.

title: normalize_team() is reused to normalize player names and nationalities, routing them through the club alias registry
evidence: soccer_data.py:722 (name), :725 (nationality), :784 (nationality) call normalize_team() on FIFA player strings. The comment at :722 admits the intent is only accent-stripping ("reuse accent-stripping"), but the function first consults CANONICAL_ALIASES, so any player/nationality string colliding with a club alias is silently rewritten (e.g. a player named "Athletico" would normalize to 'atletico pr'). Latent — no observed miscategorization in the shipped FIFA data. R7/R8 pass regardless (test_brazilian_soccer.py:256,267,279).
suggestion: Split out a plain _norm_raw()-based helper for non-team strings; keep normalize_team() for club names only.

title: Bare "Atlético" match rows are not merged into any canonical club
evidence: 10 rows across data/kaggle match CSVs carry the bare name "Atlético" with no state suffix; normalize_team() falls through to key 'atletico', which no _register() call claims, so those rows form a phantom club distinct from atletico mg/go/pr. Affects 10 of ~24k rows; does not change any pinned requirement outcome.
suggestion: Either map the bare form to its true club or exclude ambiguous bare names explicitly, and document the choice.

title: Beyond spec: explicit canonical team registry prevents Atlético-MG/GO/PR collisions
evidence: soccer_data.py:156-208 CANONICAL_ALIASES/_register() covers ~45 clubs with suffixed, bare, full-name and alternate spellings, keeping the state code in the key only to disambiguate (atletico mg vs atletico go vs atletico pr; botafogo vs botafogo pb vs botafogo sp; flamengo vs flamengo pi). Asserted by test_brazilian_soccer.py:350 test_distinct_atletico_not_merged.
suggestion: None — this is a stronger answer to TASK.md's "Implementation should normalize team names" than the spec demands.

title: Performance criteria met: store loads once via lru_cache singleton
evidence: soccer_data.py:820 @lru_cache(maxsize=1) get_store(); mcp_server.py:289 eagerly warms it in main(). Full 36-test suite including CSV load ran in 3.7s (_agent_stdout.log), well inside TASK.md's <2s simple / <5s aggregate budget for post-load queries. Loading itself uses row-wise iterrows() rather than vectorized pandas (soccer_data.py:393).
suggestion: None — vectorizing _to_unified() would cut startup but is not required.
